title: Rahul Gandhi vows to 'get rid of' Modi; BJP calls Hyderabad event 'Bharat Badnaam Summit'
dek: The Lok Sabha Opposition leader questioned the Election Commission and alleged a BJP-Adani nexus at a Telangana government-hosted summit. The BJP accused him of defaming India before foreign guests, amid a row over denied visas.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, told the closing session of the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad on Saturday that the Congress and its allies would defeat Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and said India was "actually no longer a democracy". The BJP called the event a "Bharat Badnaam Summit", or a summit to defame India, and accused him of running down the country in front of foreign delegates.

The two-day summit, its second edition, was hosted by the Congress-led Telangana government at the Hyderabad International Convention Centre. It was overshadowed before it began by a dispute over visas for foreign invitees, which the state's Chief Minister, A. Revanth Reddy, blamed on the Centre.

## What Rahul Gandhi said

"I can tell you already, with confidence, that we are going to defeat PM Modi and we are going to get rid of PM Modi," Mr Gandhi said, according to reports. He alleged that the line between business and politics had disappeared: "The line between business and politics, between Adani and PM Modi, has evaporated. It does not exist anymore."

He again questioned the Election Commission. He claimed that about 7 million voters were added in Maharashtra in the three months between the 2024 Lok Sabha and Assembly elections, and asked how an election could be legitimate if, as he put it, 140 million people who voted in 2024 were later declared non-voters. He did not give a source for these figures, and the Election Commission has previously rejected similar allegations about voter rolls. He also said the BJP's assets had grown elevenfold in a decade.

## The BJP's response

BJP spokesperson C.R. Kesavan wrote on X that the "Congress party-sponsored Bharat Summit was, in reality, a Bharat Badnaam Summit", and that Mr Gandhi had "defamed India's democratic process in front of handpicked foreign delegates". He asked the Congress to disclose the backgrounds of the foreign guests and any links to organisations funded by the investor George Soros, an allegation the BJP has made before and the Congress denies. BJP leaders in Telangana, including Union ministers G. Kishan Reddy and Bandi Sanjay Kumar, had opposed Mr Gandhi's participation.

## The visa dispute

On Friday Mr Reddy accused the Ministries of External Affairs and Home Affairs of keeping out invited speakers critical of the Prime Minister, saying visas had been refused or cancelled and that some journalists granted visas were later stopped from travelling. Congress MP Shashi Tharoor put the number at 115 of 315 speakers cleared by the External Affairs Ministry, according to reports. Mr Reddy said about 1,000 delegates from 70 countries were attending. Among those reported to have been refused was a Norwegian journalist who had asked a question about press freedom during Mr Modi's visit to Oslo in May.

Neither ministry had publicly explained the visa decisions by Sunday afternoon. Mr Gandhi apologised to the delegates who could not attend.

## What happens next

The exchange comes as the Centre weighs a special session of Parliament on delimitation and the women's reservation bill, and as the Election Commission's special revision of voter rolls continues in several states, with Uttar Pradesh's draft roll due on 17 November. Both are likely to keep the Opposition's attacks on the Commission in the headlines.
